collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — NATURE, ECOLOGY AND ANIMALS (NAT-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Isola's animals, plants, tides and weather: tide pools and nesting beaches, washed-up rubbish, shrinking clam beds, strange visitors, creatures doing what creatures do, and choices about the island where nobody gets a perfect answer.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A child finds a furry grey lump full of tiny bones under the owl's tree: take it apart together, or let it be.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Under the big tree where the owl sleeps, (subject) has found a small grey lump, furry and dry. When (subject.he/she) pulls it apart, there are tiny bones inside. Very tiny. A little skull. (subject) isn't sure if (subject.he/she) should be frightened, disgusted, or excited, and is running to (friend) to find out.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) lays it on a flat stone and teases it apart with a thorn. Owls swallow their food whole, (friend.he/she) explains, and the bits they can't use come back up in a neat little package like this. They count the bones. A mouse, they think, and maybe a beetle. (subject) decides it's the most interesting thing that has ever happened. (subject.He/she) collects owl pellets for a month. (subject.His/her) parents are less thrilled.

text_only.reason: food in the story (a meal, a catch, fruit); the village's stores do not change -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "That's what the owl had for dinner," (friend) says. "Leave it for the beetles." (subject) is a little disappointed, and a little relieved. That night (subject.he/she) lies awake and listens to the owl calling from the big tree. (subject.He/she) thinks about the mouse. (subject.He/she) thinks about the owl. (subject.He/she) decides both of them were just doing what they needed to do.
